name: IL-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: Open seat but Democratic nominee Daniel Biss well-funded with outside support
Republican challenger John Elleson with no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win near certain
model.rationale: The district's D+19 lean and an open-seat Democratic nominee who has raised nearly $3 million against a Republican with no reported fundraising make a Democratic hold overwhelmingly likely, and markets agree at roughly 97%.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Biss or an unusually favorable national Republican environment could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to flip the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jan Schakowsky (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Jan Schakowsky's retirement leaves this Chicago-area district open, but its D+19 partisan lean keeps it firmly in Democratic hands on paper. Daniel Biss, a well-known local officeholder, enters the general election with about $2.9 million raised and both outside groups supporting and opposing him active in the race. Republican John Elleson reports no fundraising figures, a stark resource gap.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, candidate finances, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at roughly 97%. The expected margin is in the low twenties, with the seat rated Safe Democratic.
